Hey y'all!

json-as 2.0.0 is here! This release brings faster generated readers, stricter opt-in validation, more reliable lazy fields and dynamic values, and a whole bunch of correctness fixes. It includes everything since v1.6.3; the planned v1.7.0 was never published.

## What’s new

- Added `JSON.validate(data)` for complete syntax validation without building a result. Opt-in `JSON_STRICT=true` builds combine validation with typed cursor parsing where supported.
- Added `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS=false` for production builds that trap on library parse failures without constructing detailed errors. Checks remain in place; detailed diagnostics are enabled by default.
- Expanded generic, alias, inheritance, lazy-field, and custom-codec support across both package entry points. ([#246](https://github.com/JairusSW/json-as/pull/246))
- Switched project code to **MPL-2.0**, with SPDX headers, retained third-party notices, and automated license checks.

## Performance

- Improved generated compact and whitespace readers, expected-order key dispatch, composite scanning, and numeric parsing. Each parse starts at the fastest tier and falls back as needed.
- Moved more schema decisions to compilation time, reduced repeated scanning and unnecessary allocation, and kept fast readers available for safe standard-library numeric defaults.
- Refreshed the [benchmark charts](https://docs.jairus.dev/json-as/guide/performance), including native-struct comparisons with simdjson and built-in JavaScript. Owning-struct serialization measures fresh output rather than forwarding a cached JSON string.

## Fixes

- Fixed numeric conversion and round-trip edges, including exact wide integers, decimal-to-float rounding, signed zero, and alias-bound floating-point fields.
- Fixed omitted defaults on reused destinations, shared-buffer overwrites, native container subclass behavior, and managed-value lifetimes during garbage collection. ([#236](https://github.com/JairusSW/json-as/pull/236), [#247](https://github.com/JairusSW/json-as/pull/247))
- Fixed lazy inheritance shadowing, declaration-scoped omission predicates, imported and default-exported models, and native-type name collisions.
- Fixed malformed token handling, nullable array elements, string escaping, static output-string reuse, and backend consistency. ([#229](https://github.com/JairusSW/json-as/pull/229), [#234](https://github.com/JairusSW/json-as/pull/234), [#242](https://github.com/JairusSW/json-as/pull/242))
- Fixed installed-package resolution in pnpm projects and workspaces by bundling xjb-as and declaring the AssemblyScript compiler peer dependency.

## Upgrading from 1.x

- Omitted fields in reused parse destinations return to their declared defaults. Present members can still reuse buffers.
- Undecorated built-in subclasses use native storage operations. Use custom codecs to customize their JSON representation.
- Dynamic numeric getters convert between numeric types using native casts. Parsed dynamic numbers use `f64`; preserve typed integer values when exact wide-integer storage matters.
- Review the [full changelog](https://github.com/JairusSW/json-as/blob/v2.0.0/CHANGELOG.md) for the complete compatibility notes and fixes.

## Testing

- The release candidate passed all eight hosted test shards, lint, and license checks.
- Packed-package checks covered both entry points, all three backends and runtimes, strict parsing on/off, and actual npm/pnpm consumer installations.
- Expanded regression coverage includes parsing, initialization, reuse, dynamic values, compiler bindings, and container subclasses.

As always, try it, break it, and tell us what feels rough!

> Join the [AssemblyScript Discord](https://discord.gg/assemblyscript/) or [open an issue](https://github.com/JairusSW/json-as/issues) with feedback. I'd love to hear how 2.0 works for you 😄
